threads.text: A proposal that's easy to say yes to is easy to forward. A short summary on page one. Always.
English and Kurdish on the same page, each in its own direction, neither one broken. In Recto any text box can run right-to-left. A small switch that saves a whole afternoon.
ڕ ڵ ێ ۆ ە. Five letters many Arabic-script fonts quietly leave out. Recto checks every Kurdish letter in the font you pick, and offers one that can set them all.
Small studios don't compete on size. They compete on attention. A client can always tell when someone actually read their brief.
Recto comes with more than 60 commercial fonts, Arabic and Kurdish faces included, ready for client work. One less licence to worry about.
Most pitch decks open with the logo, then "about us", then the team. Three slides about you before one about them. Start with them.
Hierarchy is just the answer to one question: what should they read first, what second, and what must they never skip?
Your proposal will be forwarded to someone you've never met. Design it for them too.
Open Page, weekend edition: show us a document you're proud of sending. Not the work itself. The proposal, the deck or the case study that won it.
Every Recto link shows who viewed it, how long they spent on each page and where they stopped. Clients can also pin comments to the exact spot, no account needed. Follow up with facts, not hope.
Nobody went to design school to learn how to write an invoice. And yet, here we all are.
Case study blocks in Recto come with before/after, metrics and testimonials already laid out. You bring the work. The page already knows how to show it.
Before and after is the most persuasive layout in design. Put the old next to the new, add one number, stop talking.
A4 is a desk. 16:9 is a screen. Square is a feed. Know where your document will be read before you design the first page.
A case study that works: the problem, the decision, the result. Most people skip the decision. The decision is the only part that's yours.
For years, designers here were told good work should look like it came from somewhere else. We think the most interesting brands of the next decade will look like where they're from.
Client documents are full of things that aren't public yet: prices, plans, launches. In Recto, documents are end-to-end encrypted and stay private until you publish a link. justrecto.com
The client who says "make it pop" isn't wrong. They're telling you it doesn't move them yet. Your job is to find out why, not to add a gradient.
Paste straight from Illustrator onto a Recto page. No exporting, no screenshots of your own work.
Before you hit send: how to write a scope your client can't misread.
Page numbers are a kindness. "See page 7" is a conversation. "See the slide with the blue chart" is an argument.
The best portfolios don't show everything. They show what you want to be hired for next.
Open Page: which studio, designer or writer in your city deserves more attention? Tag them. Let's give the stage away.
Most case studies show the work. The ones that win show the thinking: the problem, the decision, the result. Save it for the next one you write.
Studio rule: don't present three options when you believe in one. Three options is how you ask the client to do your job.
Clients can pin a comment to the exact spot on your page. No account, no login, no "which slide did you mean". Just a note where the problem is.
A rate card is a confidence document. If you hesitate on the number in person, put it on a page that doesn't.
Good type goes unnoticed. Bad type is the only thing anyone remembers.
Presenters: your slides are not your notes. If you can read your talk off the screen, so can the audience, and they'll do it faster than you.
Designing in two scripts on one page is a skill few design schools teach. English left to right, Kurdish right to left, both looking like they belong there. It's hard. It's worth it.
Studio notes. Ask for the deposit. Put it in the payment schedule, on its own line, before the first milestone. Clients who respect the work respect the schedule.
The deposit is not rude. The deposit is the client saying yes with their money, not just their mouth.
A Recto link opens three ways: as a magazine spread, a page-turning book or plain slides. Same document. You choose how your client meets it.
Stop sending PDFs into the void. A link tells you if they opened it, how long they stayed on the pricing page and where they stopped reading. That's not surveillance. That's knowing when to call.
A deck has one job per slide. If a slide has two jobs, it's two slides.
Writers make good clients for designers. They already know every word on the page has to earn its place.
Open Page: designers, writers, presenters. What's the strangest piece of client feedback you've ever had? Keep it anonymous. Keep it kind. Keep it funny.
Publish a Recto document as a link and choose how your client meets it: a magazine spread, a page-turning book or plain slides. Edit after sending and the link updates. justrecto.com
Freelancing is 40% design, 30% email, 20% chasing invoices and 10% wondering if you should have been an accountant.
Your logos, colours and fonts, saved once in a brand kit. Apply them to a whole document in one click. Every template in Recto starts from your brand, not ours.
